utility.notes: Silicon Valley Clean Energy's own 2020 Community Benefits Summary for Milpitas footnotes emissions figures as 'based on reported PG&E and SVCE carbon emissions factors,' consistent with PG&E remaining the underlying transmission/distribution/billing utility while SVCE is a separate default generation supplier (see generation_supplier) — the same structure independently confirmed for every other PG&E-territory CCA city this session, though this specific document does not contain an explicit 'PG&E delivers/bills' sentence the way some other cities' CCA pages do.

value.name: Silicon Valley Clean Energy (SVCE)
value.notes: Silicon Valley Clean Energy's own 2020 Community Benefits Summary states: 'In 2016, the City of Milpitas and twelve other local communities formed Silicon Valley Clean Energy (SVCE) to provide the region with clean electricity at competitive rates.' The specific default product/tier name (e.g. GreenStart vs. GreenPrime) is not stated in this document, so it is left unspecified rather than assumed.

county.notes: SVCE's own summary describes Milpitas as one of 'the City of Milpitas and twelve other local communities' that formed the county-wide Silicon Valley Clean Energy agency, structurally confirming Milpitas's place within Santa Clara County (SVCE's well-established service area).

permit_authority.value: City of Milpitas Office of Building Safety

interconnection_url.notes: Same PG&E-wide Net Energy Metering program URL already verified for other PG&E-territory records this session — reused as a utility-level fact. pge.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch; confirmed to exist via search engine indexing under its expected title.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes Milpitas/Santa Clara County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC/PG&E-administered SGIP program already verified for other PG&E-territory records this session, reused here as a utility-level fact.

SolarAPP+ PV+Battery Storage Eligibility Checklist
value.required_when: SolarAPP+ pathway, systems including battery storage

value.name: Complete set of design drawings and documents (for standard/non-SolarAPP+ submittals)
Electrical plans provided to the City inspector at the job site
value.required_when: standard permit types (ONL SOL, ONL SOL WITH PANEL)

required_documents.notes: The two SolarAPP+ eligibility checklist URLs (solarapp.nrel.gov) are the national SolarAPP+ platform's own standard checklists referenced by Milpitas's SolarAPP+ page, not a Milpitas-specific document.

value: Register and submit design at SolarAPP+ (solarapp.nrel.gov), then download the approval document
Apply for the permit online via the City of Milpitas eTRAKiT system, referencing the SolarAPP+ approval
Print the permit after payment is completed
Schedule an inspection following the City's Building Inspection Request Procedures

timeline_days.notes: No specific permit review/issuance timeline (in days) was stated on either Milpitas page reviewed this session.

value.program_or_pathway: Standard online solar permit (ONL SOL / ONL SOL WITH PANEL) or SolarAPP+
other_conditions: Standard 'ONL SOL' permit: solar panel system up to a maximum of 10kW (DC max), without electrical panel upgrade or energy storage system
'ONL SOL WITH PANEL' permit: up to 10kW (DC max) with an electrical panel upgrade up to a maximum of 200 amps
SolarAPP+ pathway separately covers systems up to 38.4kW with SolarAPP+ approval documents

eligibility_constraints.notes: Milpitas's own page states these caps explicitly as DC (unlike several other cities' AC-stated or unit-unspecified caps) — recorded under system_size_kw_dc_max rather than system_size_kw_ac_max to preserve that distinction.

permit_fees.notes: Milpitas's Solar Panel page references 'Solar Panel Permit Fees can be found in the Building Fee Schedule on page 10' but does not state a specific dollar amount on the page itself, and the fee schedule document was not located/read this session.

value.name: Lights On Silicon Valley
value.description: Additional rebate for customers who make their homes more energy resilient by installing solar plus home battery storage.
value.eligibility: SVCE residential customers installing solar + home battery storage

rebates.notes: Directly quoted from SVCE's Milpitas Community Benefits Summary: 'Customers can make their homes more energy resilient and receive an additional $1,250 in rebates when you install solar + home battery storage.' This document (dated 2020) does not state current eligibility rules, an expiration date, or whether the program is still active — status recorded as 'unknown' rather than assumed active or expired.
